name: Valid Accounts
tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
description: Adversaries obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts to gain initial access, persistence, or elevated privileges, often evading detection because the activity looks like normal user behavior.

name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries use repeated login attempts to guess credentials without prior knowledge of valid passwords.

name: Password Spraying
description: A brute-force variant using a single common password against many accounts to avoid account lockout thresholds.

name: Account Manipulation
description: Adversaries modify account permissions, group membership, or credentials to maintain access, such as adding an account to a privileged group.

name: Create Account
description: Adversaries create new accounts (local, domain, or cloud) to maintain access to a victim environment.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description: Adversaries bypass mechanisms designed to control elevated privileges, such as Windows UAC, to gain higher-level permissions.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: Adversaries exploit software vulnerabilities to elevate privileges beyond what was granted by a misconfiguration or intended access level.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Adversaries abuse command and script interpreters (PowerShell, Windows Command Shell, bash) to execute commands and payloads.

name: PowerShell
description: Adversaries abuse PowerShell for execution, often with obfuscated or encoded commands to evade detection.

name: System Binary Proxy Execution
description: Adversaries abuse trusted, signed system binaries (certutil, rundll32, regsvr32) to proxy execution of malicious payloads and evade application controls.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Adversaries encode, encrypt, or otherwise obfuscate content (e.g. base64-encoded PowerShell) to evade detection and analysis.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries transfer tools or files from an external system into a compromised environment, e.g. via download cradles.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Adversaries dump credentials (e.g. via Mimikatz) from operating system memory or storage to obtain account credentials for reuse.

name: Process Injection
description: Adversaries inject code into legitimate processes to evade defenses and elevate privileges.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Adversaries use common application-layer protocols to blend command-and-control traffic with legitimate network traffic.

name: DNS
description: Adversaries use the DNS protocol for command-and-control or data exfiltration (tunneling), often visible as high-entropy subdomain queries.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Adversaries exfiltrate data over the same channel used for command and control, rather than a separate exfiltration channel.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
description: Adversaries exfiltrate data using a different protocol than the one used for command and control, such as FTP or a non-standard port.

name: Proxy
description: Adversaries route traffic through an intermediary to obscure the true source or destination of network communications.

name: Remote Services
description: Adversaries use valid accounts to log into remote services (RDP, SMB/Windows Admin Shares) to move laterally within an environment.

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Adversaries use RDP to log into a remote host interactively as part of lateral movement.

name: Lateral Tool Transfer
description: Adversaries copy tools or files between systems in a compromised environment to support further lateral movement or execution.

name: System Services
description: Adversaries abuse system service mechanisms (e.g. PsExec-style remote service creation) to execute commands or payloads on remote hosts.

name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
description: Adversaries use stolen authentication material (e.g. password hashes) to move laterally without needing the plaintext credential (pass-the-hash).

name: Account Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate local, domain, or cloud accounts to plan further action, often preceding privilege escalation or lateral movement.

name: Remote System Discovery
description: Adversaries enumerate other systems on the network to plan lateral movement targets.
